elements.element: Customer may terminate the Agreement or an Order Form for convenience.
elements.evidence: Inserted: "Licensee may terminate this Agreement for convenience upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to Licensor". The element is disjunctive; this Agreement-level right suffices, and the document has no Order Form structure.

elements.element: Customer's convenience termination requires no more than 30 days' written notice.
elements.evidence: "upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to Licensor" — exactly 30 days, written, and no additional conditions or consent requirement attached.

elements.element: Vendor refunds prepaid fees pro rata after Customer's convenience termination.
elements.evidence: "Licensor shall refund to Licensee, pro rata, any prepaid fees for the period after the effective date of termination" — express pro rata basis, Vendor-to-Customer direction, tied to the convenience termination.

elements.element: Vendor has no right to terminate for convenience during a committed term.
elements.evidence: "Licensor shall have no right to terminate this Agreement for convenience during the Initial Period or any extension thereof." Retained Licensor rights are breach-based (Article IV), insolvency (Article XIX) and Change of Control (Article XX) — none is a convenience right; the Article IV renewal option is a RENEWAL matter.

elements.element: Customer may terminate for convenience on 60 to 90 days' notice.
elements.evidence: The inserted notice period is thirty (30) days, which sits above (better than) the fallback band but does not literally fall within 60–90 days. Only relevant if the fallback level were selected.

elements.element: Any early-termination fee is capped at three months of fees.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: no early-termination fee, penalty or accelerated-payment mechanic is imposed on Licensee's convenience termination anywhere in the rendered text, so the cap is satisfied a fortiori.

elements.element: Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: Licensor is barred from convenience termination entirely during the Initial Period or any extension, which is stricter than an end-of-term-only right.

elements.element: Vendor must give at least 90 days' notice of convenience termination.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: Licensor has no convenience termination right at all under the inserted sentence, so no notice floor is required.

reasons: Preferred level is complete: all four preferred elements are met by the single inserted sentence pair (30 days' written notice, pro rata refund of prepaid fees, and an express bar on Licensor convenience termination during the Initial Period or any extension).

Minimality holds: the insertion is a concise addition to a clause set that previously contained no Customer exit right; no existing words were deleted or paraphrased, the model-language surplus "in whole or in part" was correctly dropped (no Order Form or partial-termination structure exists), and no extras such as survival tails, expense allocation or procedural mechanics were added.

Intent is preserved: Article IV's 36-month Initial Period opens "Subject to termination pursuant to this Agreement", so the new right reads consistently; Licensor's breach termination, Article XIX insolvency rights, Article XX Change of Control auto-termination and Article XXI effect-of-termination mechanics all survive without contradiction, and no defined term or cross-reference is left dangling ("Initial Period" is a defined term used correctly).

Fallback level is incomplete only because the drafted notice period is 30 days rather than 60–90 days; that is irrelevant since the preferred level is fully met, and the margin comment's 60-day offer is correctly framed as a negotiating fallback rather than relied on as operative language.
